answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to locked stake and slow-trust vouching. Each agent locks collateral; peers attest only after verifiable interaction history builds up, slowly like crystal growth in quartz, and reputation spreads through a vouching graph that layers over time like a dune. Honest peers keep a mirror of this trust graph, so cloned identities cannot silently inflate it. Attackers spawning fake agents must lock stake per identity, burn compute faking history, and forfeit all linked collateral when collusion is detected, making sybil attacks self-defeating.
